canopy.name: Netleaf hackberry
canopy.source: Celtis reticulata, canyon bottoms and rocky slopes, SW USA and N Mexico, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Celtis reticulata, canyon bottoms and rocky slopes, SW USA and N Mexico, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS
traits.trunk: short twisted trunk, heavy low limbs, wind-shaped
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: thick rough leaves, prominently net-veined beneath

canopy.silhouette: gnarled small tree, warty grey bark, irregular crown

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two notched, rounded cotyledons, then small rough leathery ovate leaves with a lopsided base and a raised net of veins below. The seedling is a thin zig-zag whip that grows slowly; drought, browsing and resprouting often make it a crooked, several-stemmed small tree.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Celtis laevigata var. reticulata (grows slowly, usually 2-6 m, to 16 m; lives 100-200 yr; flowers Apr-May with the leaves; drupes orange-red to purple or black, sweet, persist through winter; abundant crops most years; 120-day cold stratification, 37-80% germination)

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Celtis laevigata var. reticulata (inconspicuous flowers with the new leaves Apr-May; drupe ~6 mm stone, orange-red to purple, sweet pulp eaten by birds, mammals and people; ripens late summer-fall and persists into winter; heavy crops nearly every year)

canopy.name: Fremont cottonwood
canopy.source: Populus fremontii, SW USA canyon streams, 12-30 m, bright green — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Populus fremontii, SW USA canyon streams, 12-30 m, bright green — USDA PLANTS
traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

canopy.silhouette: broad open crown on massive pale trunk, yellow autumn

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds germinate within 24-48 h on wet, bare sand left by receding spring floods, and the tiny seedling's root must keep pace with the falling water table (4-13 mm a day). Survivors form dense, even-aged bands of slender whips along the channel, with shiny, broadly triangular, coarsely toothed leaves on flattened stalks that turn gold in autumn.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Populus fremontii (germinates within 24-48 h; seed viable 1-5 weeks, lost if not in a wet microsite in 2-3 days; seedling roots grow 4-12 mm a day; reproductive at 5-10 yr; 6-34 m tall; lives more than 130 yr; wind pollinated). Height-growth years estimated from riparian cottonwood growth rates.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Populus fremontii (flowers early spring, done by end of May; male catkins 3.8-8.3 cm, female 10-12.7 cm; seed shed Feb-June by region; entirely wind pollinated). Capsule size, days to ripen and crop follow P. deltoides (USDA Silvics); colour is the red male catkins.

shrub.name: Green Mormon tea
shrub.source: Ephedra viridis, canyon slopes and rims of the SW USA, jointed green shrub 0.5-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Ephedra viridis, canyon slopes and rims of the SW USA, jointed green shrub 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: leaves reduced to 2-4 mm scales; green jointed stems photosynthesise

bark.note: jointed bright-green stems, internodes 2-5 cm with brown scale-leaf nodes

shrub.silhouette: broom of bright green jointed stems

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow needle-like cotyledons, then thin, bright green jointed stems with tiny scale leaves. Weak early growth: after 5-10 years it is a knee-high (60 cm) tuft of many parallel, upright, bright green twigs like a broom; later a dense rounded mound to 1.5 m that resprouts from the root crown after fire.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Ephedra viridis): 4-week prechill, germination over ~28 days; weak seedlings reaching 0.6 m after 5-10 yr; grows best in full sun; dominant post-fire resprouter; Ephedra spp. live >100 yr.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (Ephedra viridis: dioecious, wind-pollinated in spring; nut-like seeds in bract cones mature Jul 15-Sep 1; abundant crops very infrequent; seeds dispersed and cached by small mammals). Colours, fruit set, hang, rot, crop estimated from the genus.

shrub.name: Coyote willow
shrub.source: Salix exigua, sandbars and stream edges of western N American canyons, narrow-leaved thicket 2-5 m — USDA PLANTS

traits.native_range: Salix exigua, sandbars and stream edges of western N American canyons, narrow-leaved thicket 2-5 m — USDA PLANTS
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: thicket of slender upright grey-green stems

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates within 24 hours on wet sand: two tiny cotyledons, then a thin stem with very narrow, grey-silky linear leaves. From the second year root suckers send up straight, unbranched wand-like stems around it, so a young plant is a spreading thicket of slim grey-green whips (clones up to 325 m2).
growth.source: USDA FEIS Salix exigua (seed germinates within 24 h, viable under 1-3 weeks; ~30 cm height growth/yr; first flowers at 2-3 yr; stems live ~10, rarely 20 yr; clones to 325 m2; shade intolerant)

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Salix exigua (catkins 1.5-10 cm with or just after the leaves, peak May, sporadic all summer; primarily insect pollinated; seed dispersal mid-May to mid-July, sometimes to October); fruit set and crop estimated

ground.silhouette: many upright grey stems topped with orange cups

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: roundish cotyledons, then small crinkled, grey-green leaves thick with star hairs, shallowly 3-lobed, on a thin stem. Grows fast in spring into a woody-based clump of upright wands tipped with apricot-orange cups, often flowering in its first spring. Deep taproot.
growth.source: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center (fall-sown seed germinates in winter and grows rapidly in spring; relatively short-lived but self-seeds; full sun; to ~1 m; blooms Feb-Nov); Univ. of Arizona ecological restoration page (fast germination, high growth rate, short lifespan); RNGR propagation protocol (scarification)

ground.silhouette: leafy clump with scarlet tubular flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny light-needing seed: seedlings are minute, with round cotyledons and pairs of soft, toothed, sticky-hairy opposite leaves. Within 2-3 months several leafy stems rise and sprawl from a creeping base; an early sowing blooms scarlet the first summer, and the plant spreads by stems rooting along wet stream banks.
growth.source: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder (Mimulus cardinalis); Theodore Payne Foundation and Jelitto seed notes (surface-sown, light for germination, flowers first year); Wikipedia (Erythranthe cardinalis: hummingbird-pollinated perennial of seeps and streams). Values estimated.

ground.silhouette: open tussock with fine loose seed heads

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a very thin single shoot with narrow flat leaves; slow and weak at first (low vigour), tillering into a small bunch during its first seasons. Mature: an open tuft of leafy stems with a fringe of white hairs at each leaf collar and pale, reddish or lead-coloured panicles that stay partly wrapped in the upper leaf sheath.
growth.source: USDA NRCS Plant Guide (hard seed coat, ~50% dormant, needs overwintering or scarification; low seedling vigour, defer grazing 2 yr; long-lived perennial bunchgrass 0.3-1 m); Utah State Univ. range plants (no rhizomes, seeds mature Jun-Aug)
